scope: Verification-only composition of A1 machine identity, A2 authority manifest, optional A3a attenuation proof, and A4a signed handoff. The live verifier rechecks supplied artifacts; the detached report checker only checks report self-consistency because the report itself is unsigned.
core_invariant: Artifact verification and report integrity are different assurances. Only a live verifyAgentTrustBundle call may say the supplied A1/A2/A3a/A4a artifacts were reverified. A detached content-addressed report is unauthenticated and cannot prove that verification actually occurred.

risks: swap A1 credential
swap A2 manifest
swap A4 handoff
pair valid artifacts from different principals or snapshots
controls: A2 independently reproduces A1 principal/credential binding
live bundle verifier exposes target/input expected checks

risks: attacker fabricates an unsigned report and recomputes its digest
detached report digest mistaken for proof that underlying artifacts were verified
controls: only live bundle result returns underlying_artifacts_reverified=true

risks: recipient name/digest rebound
executor name/digest rebound
input or causal parent changed
controls: A4 expected recipient/executor identity, input and parent checks are exposed through A10a
live report records exact target/input fields

risks: A3a proof interpreted as parent delegation authority
proof attached to A4a as delegation chain
synthetic positive attenuation treated as runtime delegation
controls: A3a verification is optional and labeled proof_only

risks: unsigned report changed to authority/currentness/success claims
report metadata changed to self-signed or portable assurance
verifier gains private-key generation/signing
verifier creates authority artifacts
verifier performs filesystem/network/process effects
controls: verifier implementation imports only canonicalization plus verify primitives
static regression forbids crypto/fs/process/network and artifact-creation APIs

risks: historical A1/A2/A4 validity treated as globally current
absence of A6 revocation evidence treated as active authority
same-repository verifier bundle described as a separately implemented third-party verifier
conformance bundle marketed as cross-vendor proof
controls: A10a explicitly uses canonical AXIOM verifier primitives
runtime-separated/public-input and independently implemented conformance remain later gates

known_nonclaims: A10a is not a separately implemented third-party verifier; it composes canonical AXIOM verify primitives.
The unsigned verification report is not portable proof that verification occurred; its digest proves self-consistency only.
A10a does not verify A5 portable work receipts yet.
A10a does not establish live revocation/currentness or delegation authority.
A10a does not authorize or execute the A4 handoff.
A10a does not prove legal identity, task success, effect execution, application correctness, or truth.
A10a does not expose MCP/A2A/network effects or modify capability-registry state.
next_gates: A10b extend live verification to a green A5 portable work receipt chain
A10c runtime-separated verifier process/package accepting public verification inputs only
A10d independently implemented conformance harness or second implementation
A9 cross-protocol parity fixtures proving native/MCP/A2A adapters preserve identical authority semantics
